mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not statistically significant at p < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over the same month indicates a housing demand shock with weak overall demand, which depresses consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 0% monthly change AND GDPC1 < 0% monthly change
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the interaction term's coefficient is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy with falling inflation, which typically supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND CPIAUCSL < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the positive rank IC is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above 0.4% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the positive rank IC is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 2% for four consecutive months signals a surge in household savings, which often coincides with precautionary behavior and reduced consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 2% monthly change for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.10.
